solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Brandy — not quite enough for the month

indicators.note: something not quite enough falls a little short, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: March is the third month of the year

explanation.surface: Someone complains there is too little brandy to last the month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite enough' cuts the last letter, H, from MARCH.
explanation.definitionFit: Marc is a French spirit distilled from grape pressings, a kind of brandy.

clue.text: Material adding weight to bottom of bed

indicators.note: in a down answer, the second piece is added below the first, at its bottom

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
a ton is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: A fabric that makes the underside of a bed heavier.
explanation.definitionFit: Cotton is a common woven fabric, so it is a material.

clue.text: Changeable island that gets cold I love — and not just me on my own!

parts.note: Capri is an island in the Bay of Naples
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
taken as written
love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O

parts.words: not just me on my own
parts.note: not just me but others too: the pronoun for a group including the speaker

explanation.surface: A fickle island where the cold gets to the speaker and others alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Capricious describes moods or behaviour that change suddenly and unpredictably.

clue.text: Monster appears — ship therefore capsizes

indicators.note: in a down answer a capsized vessel is turned upside down, so the whole run is read bottom to top

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
ergo is Latin for therefore

explanation.surface: A sea monster rises up and so the vessel overturns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capsizes' turns SSERGO round to give OGRESS.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogress is a female ogre, a monstrous giant of folk tales.

clue.text: Article that's a nuisance crushing a foot

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: one word crushing another squeezes it inside

parts.note: a pest is an annoying nuisance

explanation.surface: Someone describes an irritating object that lands heavily on a foot.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'a' sits inside PEST to make PAEST. 'foot' is the metrical unit, not the body part.
explanation.definitionFit: An anapaest is a metrical foot of two short syllables followed by a long one.

clue.text: Alternatively a learner will get a test

parts.note: or introduces an alternative
L is the learner plate on British cars

explanation.surface: A trainee driver faces some kind of examination.
explanation.definitionFit: An oral is a spoken examination, a common kind of test.

clue.text: Thunderous character in request for superabundance

indicators.note: one piece sits in the other

parts.note: a plea is an earnest request
Thor is the Norse god of thunder

explanation.surface: A loud figure is begging for far too much of something.
explanation.definitionFit: A plethora is an excess or overabundance of something.

clue.text: Attractive woman? I nab 'er, reportedly!

indicators.note: as it would be said, signalling words that sound like other words

parts.note: to nab someone is to catch them, and 'er is a dropped-aitch her

explanation.surface: A man boasts of grabbing a pretty woman.
explanation.definitionFit: An eye-catcher is someone striking who draws attention, here a glamorous woman.

clue.text: Fragrance brought about by 'glamor' (American)

indicators.note: brought about is the sailing term for turning round, so the letters run backwards
the letters are found by, that is within, the quoted words

explanation.surface: A perfume is credited to American-spelt glamour.
explanation.walkthrough: In GLAMORAMERICAN the run AMORA is held inside; 'brought about' turns it to give the fragrance.
explanation.definitionFit: An aroma is a pleasant smell, a synonym for fragrance.

clue.text: All energy will get dissipated in the normal run of things

definitions.text: in the normal run of things

indicators.note: scattered or dispersed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Energy is usually lost as things run their course.
explanation.definitionFit: Generally means usually or as a rule, describing what happens ordinarily.

clue.text: Firm has obligation to entertain top lady in camp

parts.note: Co is short for company, a firm

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to take them in, so one piece holds another

parts.note: a tie is a binding obligation
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A company obliged to host the monarch at a campsite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'camp' is a faction or side, not tents.
explanation.definitionFit: A camp in the sense of a set of like-minded people is a clique or exclusive circle.

clue.text: Nearly all coppers admitting it would be prudent

indicators.note: letting in, so one piece goes inside the other
nearly all of a word means its last letter goes

parts.note: coppers is slang for police officers

explanation.surface: It would be wise for almost all the police to confess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nearly all' turns POLICE into POLIC, which then takes in IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Politic means shrewd and sensible in the circumstances, so wise or prudent.

clue.text: Like a big boom, so pleasant when it finishes prematurely!

indicators.note: ending early, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: nice means pleasant

explanation.surface: A loud bang is quite agreeable if it stops early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when it finishes prematurely' turns NICE into NIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Sonic means relating to sound, as with a sonic boom.

clue.text: Squeals when catching cold — money lost!

indicators.note: one piece catches, or holds, the other inside it

parts.note: to squeal or sing is criminal slang for informing
a chill is a cold

explanation.surface: Someone shrieks on catching a chill and losing their cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Squeals' is informing to the police, not screaming.
explanation.definitionFit: The schilling was Austria's currency until the euro replaced it, so it is money no longer used.

clue.text: Tomb at sea? It could be if it capsizes!

definitions.text: Tomb at sea? It could be if it capsizes!

indicators.note: overturned, so the letters are tumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A vessel could become a watery grave if it overturns.
explanation.definitionFit: A steamboat that sinks would become a tomb at sea for those aboard.

clue.text: Weapon that could be menacing, uh?

indicators.note: the letters could be rearranged into another word

explanation.surface: A weapon that might look threatening, asks someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine gun is an automatic firearm, a weapon.

clue.text: Doctor to approach — I itch — he should know all about that!

definitions.text: Doctor to approach — I itch — he should know all about that!

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with or alter, so the letters are changed round

explanation.surface: A patient goes to the doctor about an itch, as a physician bound by duty should help.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hippocratic oath is the ethical pledge doctors take, so every physician knows it.

clue.text: One's thinking 'possible swimming site'? Then there's double hesitation

parts.note: a pond is a place one might swim

indicators.note: doubled, so the piece is given twice

parts.note: er is a sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Someone muses about a swimming spot and keeps hesitating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's thinking' is a noun phrase: one who is thinking.
explanation.definitionFit: A ponderer is a person who thinks deeply, one who ponders.

clue.text: Coming down to be listened to like a king or a queen

definitions.text: like a king or a queen

indicators.note: heard rather than read, so the word is one that sounds like another

parts.note: rain coming down means it is raining

explanation.surface: A monarch descends to hear their subjects.
explanation.definitionFit: A reigning monarch is one currently on the throne, as kings and queens are.

clue.text: Country's left with inadequate notion — possible result of election

parts.note: land is country, with the possessive s

indicators.note: falling short, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: an idea is a notion

explanation.surface: A nation left with a half-formed plan, as might follow an election.
explanation.definitionFit: A landslide is an overwhelming victory in an election.

clue.text: Looking after number one, leader set off being mischievous

indicators.note: the leader, the first letter, is sent away

parts.note: looking after number one means putting oneself first

explanation.surface: Self-interest leads someone into playing tricks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader set off' drops the S from SELFISH.
explanation.definitionFit: Elfish means like an elf, impish and full of pranks.

clue.text: Conclude wearing what an ethical person wouldn't wear, as they say

parts.note: dressed in something, so in

indicators.note: as people say it, so the word sounds like the letters needed

parts.words: what an ethical person wouldn't wear
parts.note: animal fur is shunned by ethically minded dressers

explanation.surface: Someone decides on clothing a principled person would avoid.
explanation.definitionFit: To infer is to reach a conclusion by reasoning, so to deduce.

clue.text: Scraps left to be wasted in plane journeys

indicators.note: wasted, lost, so the letter is removed

parts.note: flights are journeys by plane

explanation.surface: Leftover food is thrown away on aeroplane trips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scraps' is the verb-turned-noun for fights, not leftovers.
explanation.definitionFit: Scraps are informal fights or brawls.

clue.text: One has to exist with exceptional rain in part of Europe

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
to be is to exist

indicators.note: out of the ordinary, so the letters are taken in an unusual order

explanation.surface: Someone has to live with unusually heavy rain in a European region.
explanation.definitionFit: Iberian describes the peninsula of Spain and Portugal, a region of Europe.

clue.text: Interested in religious books, I love to collect such

indicators.note: to collect something is to gather it in, so one piece takes in the other

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O
NT is the New Testament

explanation.surface: A collector of religious texts declares their passion.
explanation.definitionFit: To be into something is informal for being keen on or interested in it.

clue.text: Goods about to be packed in box

indicators.note: one piece is packed inside the other

parts.note: to box is to fight
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Merchandise is packed into a crate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'box' is the verb to fight, not a container.
explanation.definitionFit: Freight is goods carried by ship, train or lorry.

clue.text: Dish from the beginning but not the beginning

indicators.note: dropping the beginning, the first letter

parts.note: from the start, so the word start

explanation.surface: A dish made from scratch, with the first part left out.
explanation.definitionFit: A tart is a pastry dish with a filling.

clue.text: See new singer get a word of welcome

indicators.note: made new, so the letters form a fresh word

explanation.surface: Look, a new vocalist is welcomed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' just tells the solver to look; it gives no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Greetings is an exclamation used to welcome someone.

clue.text: Express an opinion that's absolute

definitions.meaning: to voice or say something aloud
complete or total, as in a total fool

explanation.definitionFit: Utter means both to speak words and complete or total as an adjective.
